prompt: coreutils chroot newroot identical old root directory behavior
answer:
When `newroot` is identical to the current (old) `/` directory, GNU Coreutils `chroot` avoids calling the `chroot` system call. This provides consistency with systems where changing to the same root is permitted for non-privileged users.

In this case, `--skip-chdir` is permitted and can preserve the existing working directory instead of changing it to `/`. [GNU Coreutils `chroot` documentation](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/chroot)
